blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A PodDisruptionBudget limits how many Pods may be evicted at once. It comes from the policy/v1 API.
blocks.why: Node upgrades and repairs evict Pods. A budget keeps enough of them running meanwhile.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a PodDisruptionBudget, from the policy/v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: You use the name to check how many evictions it allows right now.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the budget
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: web-pdb

blocks.title: Which Pods?
blocks.what: The selector picks the Pods labelled app: web, the Pods from the Deployment lesson.
blocks.why: The budget protects only Pods that match. It must use the same label as the Deployment.
blocks.ifRemoved: The budget protects no Pods, so a drain can evict them all.
blocks.comment: Protect the Pods labelled app: web
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: web-pdb
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web

blocks.title: How many may go?
blocks.what: maxUnavailable: 1 lets at most one web Pod be evicted at a time.
blocks.why: With two replicas, one Pod keeps serving while the other moves. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes accepts the budget, but it allows no voluntary evictions at all.
blocks.comment: At most one web Pod may be evicted at a time
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: web-pdb
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  maxUnavailable: 1

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Budgets are in policy/v1.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A PodDisruptionBudget limits evictions.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The budget’s name, used with kubectl get pdb.
notes.spec: The desired state: which Pods to protect, and how many may go at once.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be protected.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: Protect Pods labelled app: web, the Deployment lesson’s Pods.
notes.spec.maxUnavailable: At most one protected Pod may be evicted at a time. minAvailable is the alternative.

tryIt.result: Starts the two web Pods from the Keep your app running lesson.
ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS shows 1 once both web Pods are ready.
The NODE column shows where each web Pod runs. Note a node with a web Pod.
Evicts one web Pod, then is refused for the next: Cannot evict pod as it would violate the pod’s disruption budget. One node cannot run the replacement, so drain stops after 30 seconds.

expect: Cannot evict pod as it would violate the pod's disruption budget.

tryIt.result: Lets Pods start on the node again, so the evicted web Pod comes back.
ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS returns to 1 once both Pods are ready again.
Removes the budget and the Deployment.

questions.question: The Deployment runs two web Pods. How many can a drain evict at the same time?
questions.explain: maxUnavailable: 1 allows one eviction at a time. The next waits until a replacement is ready.

questions.question: Does the budget stop kubectl delete pod?
answers: No, it only limits evictions, such as a drain
Only for Pods labelled app: web
questions.explain: Deleting a Pod directly skips the budget. Drains and node upgrades use evictions, which respect it.

questions.question: With two replicas, which line could replace line 9 and allow the same evictions?
questions.explain: Keeping at least one of two Pods is the same as letting at most one go.

fix.explain: The selector looks for app: wbe, but the Pods are labelled app: web. The budget protects nothing, so a drain could evict every Pod.
fix.fix: Match the Deployment’s label exactly: app: web.
